description: BackgroundOcular manifestations are under-recognized complications of expanded dengue syndrome, with no robust frequency estimates available.MethodsA systematic review was conducted following PRISMA guidelines. Primary studies reporting the frequency of ocular manifestations consistent with expanded dengue syndrome (uveitis, maculopathy, retinal hemorrhage, retinal vasculitis, and optic neuropathy) in patients with confirmed dengue diagnosis were included.

title: Single-cell mapping of thymus-dependent naïve t-cell regeneration reveals CD61-associated states after hematopoietic stem cell transplantation
creator: Fangqing Zhang, Xinya Jiang, Shuang Fan, Bixia Wang, Zhigui Wu, Jingrui Zhou, Qi Zhang, Zhiyu Zhang, Jianing Tang, Zheng-Li Xu, Yu Wang, Xiao-Jun Huang, Huidong Guo
description: Thymus-dependent de novo T-cell generation is essential for maintaining T-cell diversity and immune competence. Although thymic involution after puberty reduces thymic output, residual thymic function remains important for immune surveillance and immune reconstitution following hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT). However, the cellular features that distinguish thymus-derived naïve T cells from those maintained through peripheral homeostatic expansion remain poorly understood.

title: The role of classical protein tyrosine phosphatases in diabetic kidney disease and therapeutic implications
creator: Grace LeBleu, Fawaz G Haj
description: Approximately one-third of people with diabetes have diabetic kidney disease (DKD), and DKD remains a leading cause of kidney failure in the United States. DKD is characterized by injury to the glomerular filtration barrier and renal tubulointerstitium, arising from complex and convergent metabolic, hemodynamic, and inflammatory insults.

title: Home health care, e-health, and telemedicine policies in selected middle and high-income countries: a rapid policy review
creator: Jesus Felix Valenzuela, Mia Desiree Verdeprado, Abigail Tan, Kristine Ann Carandang, Michael Dorosan, Christian Alis
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Home health care (HHC) is the provision and delivery of health care services where patients live. In this work, with the Philippines as an exemplar for lower-middle income countries in a similar situation (young-skewing demographics, fragmented health care system, and nascent HHC sector), we review policies regarding HHC services, telehealth, and e-Health in the Philippines and seven other jurisdictions (USA, UK, Canada, Australia, EU, Malaysia, and Thailand), identify specific “best-practice” policies covering aspects such as service delivery, personnel training, financing and governance,

title: Structural requirements for intelligent clinical digital twins in feedback-driven care
creator: Yanfei Wang, Glenn E. Smith, Gloria P. Lipori, Ramon C. Sun, Elizabeth A. Shenkman, Mei Liu, Yonghui Wu, Yi Guo
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Clinical digital twins are increasingly promoted for decision support, yet most are designed and validated for prediction under observed care rather than decision-support validity. We identify four structural requirements for intelligent clinical digital twins used in bidirectional clinical care. Using Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias as an example, we show how routine deployment can induce care-path-dependent epistemic drift despite stable predictive performance.

title: Reference quality of OpenEvidence across five medical specialties
creator: Tamir Lotan, Mahmud Omar, Yiftach Barash, Jonathan B. Kruskal, Muneeb Ahmed, Olga R. Brook, Eyal Klang, Alon Gorenshtein
description: OpenEvidence (OE) is a retrieval-augmented clinical AI tool. We evaluated the references OE returned to 150 standardized prompts across five specialties, analyzing all 4979 citations. No reference was confirmed as fabricated; three abstracts had attribution errors. Most references were recent and high-impact, though journal concentration varied by specialty.

title: In vivo adaptive optics retinal imaging reveals rod-mediated cone photoreceptor disorganization in RHO-associated retinitis pigmentosa
creator: Annette Kaminaka, Tao Liu, John P. Giannini, Natalie Toth, Diego Dominguez, Nancy Aguilera, Furu Zhang, Joanne Li, Bin Guan, Brett G. Jeffrey, Alfredo Dubra, Wadih M. Zein, Laryssa A. Huryn, Johnny Tam
description: Pathogenic variants in the rhodopsin (RHO) gene are the most common cause of autosomal dominant retinitis pigmentosa leading to photoreceptor degeneration. Quantitative imaging using adaptive optics (AO) revealed irregularities in cone organization, even in relatively well-preserved retinal locations. At the leading disease front, rod density was disrupted to a greater extent than cones.

title: Creating bottom-up RNA transfer vehicles from synthetic protein assemblies
creator: Maren Kirstin Schuhmacher, Christoph Gruber, Christopher M R Lang, Ricardo M W Ruijpers, Lyupka Mazneykova, Brice Beinsteiner, Ariane Krus, Barbara Tremmel, Friederike Reinhardt, Karoline Kadletz, Zhe Ma, Lucie Casalta, Josep Miquel Cambra Bort, Dina Y Otify, Iolo Balken, Leon Hetzel, Juliane Merl-P
description: Evolution guides biological systems to populate ecological niches, with viruses among the most successful examples of this principle. Viruses evolved over billions of years to efficiently transfer genetic information. Although viruses are highly diverse, most have converged towards remarkable similarity in the size and shape of their capsids1,2.

title: Efficacy of a self-guided online resilience intervention for improving mental health among university students: A randomized controlled trial
creator: Sonja Bartelt, Tabea Werner, Lisa von Boros, Sarah K Schäfer, Friederike Koehler, Benedikt E Wirth, Klaus Lieb, Oliver Tüscher, Michèle Wessa
description: Epidemiological data indicates that university students are an at-risk population for the development of mental disorders. Online interventions have been proposed as promising tools for reducing barriers to treatment and establishing easily accessible health-care services promoting mental health and resilience. This study investigated the efficacy of a Learning Management System (LMS)-based self-guided online resilience intervention.

title: Bridging primary care with artificial intelligence: toward a global 1.5-Tier Healthcare System
creator: Se Young Jung, Seong-Ho Han, Eojin Yi, Wooin Seo, Yeonsoo Kang, Sang Min Park, Jiho Cha
description: Artificial intelligence is increasingly applied in primary care, yet systematic frameworks linking individual applications to health-system improvement remain lacking. This perspective proposes a “1.5-Tier Healthcare System,” in which AI forms an intermediary layer between primary and specialist care, strengthening its four core functions: first contact, comprehensiveness, coordination, and continuity.

title: A curated benchmark for cofolding models on kinase conformational states
creator: Kunyang Sun, Teresa Head-Gordon
description: Protein kinases are critical drug targets, requiring therapeutics that can modulate their active and inactive conformational states. While cofolding models can generate global folds directly from kinase sequences and ligand SMILES strings, these models have not yet been tested on their ability to recover ligand-induced-fit conformational states of the kinase proteins.

title: Retraction Note: FTIR based assessment of microplastic contamination in soil water and insect ecosystems reveals environmental and ecological risks
creator: S Rathikannu, Sneha Gautam, Suneel Kumar Joshi, Praveena Katharine, K E Mithra, P Banusaranya, V M Amudhavarshini, R Gayatri, Chang-Hoi Ho
description: re raised regarding inadequate reporting of the FTIR methodology, particularly the polymer identification criteria, use of standards for method validation, and quality control details. Additionally, the spectra data presented in Figures 4, 5, and 6 do not contain peaks consistent with the reported identification of polyethylene, polystyrene, and polypropylene.

title: Data driven selection of consensus docking pipelines for structure based hit identification
creator: Hamza Agha, Youssef Ibrahim, Michael Backenköhler, Antoine Lacour, Mostafa M. Hamed, Anna K. H. Hirsch, Andrea Volkamer
description: Structure-based virtual screening (SBVS) is a cornerstone of computer-aided drug design, yet its success depends on selecting a combination of docking tools, scoring function (SF), and ranking strategies. MolDockLab addresses this challenge with an automated, data-driven framework that optimizes SBVS workflows for a protein target, balancing predictive performance and computational efficiency.

title: A novel use of AI for prediction of clinical deterioration in a post-acute hospital
creator: Alexander Kauffman, Nataša Lazarević, Rahul Joshi, Jordan Pelc
description: There is a growing literature on the prediction of risk of deterioration in hospital settings, including by leveraging artificial intelligence (AI) models. However, this literature has focused on acute-care hospitals, rather than post-acute facilities, where the risk of deterioration remains high.

title: Resin does not safeguard insect DNA during early decay despite preservation of soft tissues
creator: David Peris, Anabela Cardoso, Bastian Mähler, Sabina Karačić, Josefa Cruz, Xavier Franch-Marro, David Martín, Enrique Peñalver, Mónica M Solórzano-Kraemer, Atahualpa S Kraemer, Antonio Monleón-Getino, Xavier Delclòs, Ricardo Pérez-de la Fuente, Alba Sánchez-García, Sergio Álvarez-Parra, Jörg U Hamme
description: The notion that plant resin acts as an exceptional preservative of insect DNA and soft tissues—functioning as a natural dehydration capsule—has been questioned in recent years, yet empirical support remains limited. We applied an actuotaphonomic approach across a 30-day time series to assess DNA and internal soft tissue preservation in two model species of insects, i.e.

title: Programmable hydrodynamics of active particles
creator: Lisa Rohde, Gordei Anchutkin, Viktor Holubec, Frank Cichos
description: Self-propelled microparticles create flow fields that determine how they interact with surfaces, external flows, and each other. These flow fields fall into distinct classes–pushers, pullers, and neutral swimmers–each exhibiting fundamentally different collective behaviors. In all existing synthetic systems, this hydrodynamic character is permanently set during fabrication.

title: Reciprocal, methylation-dependent binding of Zfp57 and Gzf1 safeguards Dlk1-Dio3 imprinting during developmental reprogramming
creator: Arik Toren, Liron Hoffman, Irina Miodownik, Yoav Mayshar, Raz Ben-Yair, Ayelet-Hashahar Orenbuch, Hernan Rubinstein, Aviezer Lifshitz, Roni Stok Ranen, Alexander Wainstein, Daoud Sheban, Liran Shlush, Amos Tanay, Ariel Afek, Yonatan Stelzer
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Genomic imprinting secures parent-specific gene expression through differential DNA methylation at imprinted control regions (ICRs). However, how unmethylated alleles resist de novo methylation remains unclear. Using an allelic Dlk1-Dio3 ICR methylation reporter and genome-wide loss-of-function screening, we identify the zinc finger protein GZF1 that binds the unmethylated maternal ICR and protects it from de novo methylation via a regulatory element containing GZF1 and ZFP57 motifs that mediates mutually exclusive, methylation-dependent binding.

title: Regulatory mechanisms of maternal imprinting at the murine Dlk1-Dio3 domain
creator: Ariella Weinberg-Shukron, Frances L Dearden, Ana Moreno-Barriga, Lok Ting Nick New, Marco Müller, Rebecca C Rancourt, Carol A Edwards, Anne C Ferguson-Smith
description: Genomic imprinting is an epigenetic process causing parent-of-origin specific gene expression. The Dlk1-Dio3 domain is one of the largest imprinted clusters. While DNA methylation at an intergenic CpG-island (IG-CGI) within the imprinting control region (ICR) controls expression from the paternal chromosome, mechanisms regulating the unmethylated maternal chromosome remain unknown.

title: Identification and validation of central amygdala FGFR1 as a therapeutic target for alcohol use disorder using single-nucleus sequencing in rats
creator: Estelle Barbier, Leon Höglund, Li Xu, Nihal A Salem, Elizabeth A Osterndorff-Kahanek, Riccardo Barchiesi, Antonio Lacorte, Lief E Fenno, Robert O Messing, R Dayne Mayfield, Markus Heilig
description: A significant minority of alcohol users develop alcohol addiction, characterized by continued use despite negative consequences, referred to as compulsive-like. We previously showed that vulnerability to compulsive-like alcohol use can be modeled in rats using punished alcohol self-administration and in male rats is mediated by PKCδ+ neurons in the central nucleus of the amygdala (CeA).

title: Self-organization of vascularized muscle from bovine embryonic stem cells
creator: Marina Sanaki-Matsumiya, Yuya Sanaki, Casandra Villava, Luca Rappez, Nicola Gritti, Fumio Nakaki, James Sharpe, Kristina Haase, Jun Wu, Miki Ebisuya
description: Cultured beef offers a promising alternative to traditional meat. While adult stem cells are commonly used as the cell source for cultured beef, their proliferation and differentiation capacities are limited. Current manufacturing processes for cultured beef steaks often require separate preparation of multiple cell types and their intricate assembly.

title: Mechano-metabolic axis involves mitochondrial responses via BMP/Smad regulatory effect on cyclophilin D
creator: Rubens Sautchuk, Josaranie Nieves Santana, Chen Yu, Hani Awad, Roman A Eliseev
description: Mechanical stimulation is fundamental for anabolism in various tissues, including bone. Importantly, mechanical stimulation has been shown to induce reprogramming of cell metabolism, likely to adjust it to increased anabolism. The signal transduction within this mechano-metabolic axis is incompletely understood. Aiming to delineate such signal transduction, we exposed osteoprogenitors to fluid shear stress (FSS) and assessed cell signaling and bioenergetics.

title: Trends in the Proportion of People Who Eat Out More than Once a Day, 2013–2022
creator: Unknown
description: a day by age, 2022 Footnotes *Proportion of people who eat out more than once a day: proportion of people who eat out more than once a day, among those aged 1 year and over. †The mean in Figure 1 was calculated using age- and sex-specific structures of the estimated population in the 2005 Korea Census.

title: Trends in the Prevalence of Perceived Depressive Symptoms among Korean Adolescents, 2014–2023
creator: Unknown
description: ilar (Figures 1, 2). Trends in the prevalence of perceived depressive symptoms by gender, 2014–2023 Trends in the prevalence of perceived depressive symptoms by school levels, 2014–2023 Footnotes *Prevalence of perceived depressive symptoms: the percentage of students who experienced such extreme sorrow or despair to the extent of withdrawing from daily life for 2 weeks.

title: 1:1 observation and support: a quality improvement approach to reducing cost and improving therapeutic input
creator: David Thomas, Marie Little, Jessica Pawley
description: Our quality improvement (QI) project aimed to reduce reliance on external temporary staff used for 1:1 observation and support within a recently merged acute, community and mental health National Health Service (NHS) Trust. Temporary staffing costs reached £2.7 million in the previous financial year.

title: Bioprospecting and phylogenetic analysis of Priestia flexa AW3: an industrially significant amylase-producing bacterium from unexplored contaminated soil in Layyah
creator: Sobia Ramzan, Musrat Shaheen, Mohsin Khurshid, Farhat Jabeen, Sara Mahmood, Ayesha Sarwar, Shahzad Ahmad
description: In spite of wonderful industrial applications of microbial enzymes, still most of habitats in various parts of world are unexplored for bioprospecting of industrial potent microbes. This study represents the first bioprospecting effort in Layyah district to explore indigenous bacterial diversity, enzymatic potential, and phylogenetic relationships in untapped contaminated soil habitat.

title: Targeting the PD-L1-induced PDK4/GLS metabolic axis overcomes anti-PD-1 resistance in non-small cell lung cancer
creator: Wenxin Lian, Hui Yang, Yuqi Zhang, Chenchen Liu, Chunyao Fang, Mengyue Xu, Yixing Yang, Yan Wang, Runqiu Jiang, Jing Xu, Wen Gao
description: BackgroundMetabolic reprogramming within the tumor microenvironment is a pivotal barrier to effective immune checkpoint blockade (ICB). While programmed death ligand 1 (PD-L1) is well characterized as a ligand inhibiting T-cell function, its intrinsic ‘reverse signaling’ role in regulating tumor metabolism and shaping the immune landscape remains poorly understood.

title: Markov Decision Process–Based Personalized Follow-Up Planning for Type 2 Diabetes: Retrospective Cohort Study
creator: Silei Chen, Tianyi Liu, Zhonghua Sun, Jian Jia, Dong Hang, Wenhong Zhang
description: BackgroundPersonalized follow-up for type 2 diabetes may improve the alignment between monitoring intensity and patient needs, but operational approaches that jointly consider follow-up timing, modality, expected health benefits, and resource use remain limited.ObjectiveThis study develops a Markov decision process (MDP) framework for personalized follow-up planning, externally validates complementary risk-prediction models, and estimates the projected 12-month cost-effectiveness of model-generated follow-up strategies.

title: Decoding cancer with artificial intelligence: Transforming research, diagnosis, and therapy with future insights
creator: Muneera Anwer, Krupa Bhaliya, Ming Q Wei
description: Highlights•Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming the cancer research from drug discovery and biomarker identification to diagnosis and therapy.•Deep learning frameworks accelerate oncology drug discovery and repurposing, reducing timelines and costs through predictive modelling and molecular simulation.•Multi-omics integration powered by AI enables the discovery of robust biomarkers for diagnosis, prognosis, and therapy response prediction.

title: Are more otolaryngologists enough to improve surgical access? Geographic distribution and health system barriers in Brazil
creator: Lucas Sousa Salgado, Sofia Fontes de Oliva, Rebecca Gallardo Franco de Andrade, Vagner Antonio Rodrigues Silva, Arthur Menino Castilho
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectiveTo examine the geographic distribution of otolaryngologists in Brazil and evaluate the association between specialist density and otolaryngologic surgical provision within the public health system between 2008 and 2024.MethodsThis nationwide longitudinal study used data from the Hospital Information System of the Brazilian Unified Health System (SIH/SUS), combined with demographic and economic indicators obtained from the Brazilian Institute of Geography and Statistics. Otolaryngologist workforce density was defined as the number of practicing specialists per 100,000 inhabitants in each state.

title: RELATIONSHIP OF IMMUNOHISTOCHEMICAL EXPRESSION OF CD86/CD163 POSITIVE INTRATUMORAL MACROPHAGES WITH PROGNOSIS OF PANCREATIC DUCTAL ADENOCARCINOMA
creator: Goran Glavčić, Mario Zovak, Slavica Sović, Silvija Mašić, Nina Blažević, Zvonimir Misir, Zdenko Bilić, Marin Glavčić, Petra Radulović
description: SUMMARYRecent studies have shown an association of the number of tumor-associated macrophages (TAM) with the prognosis and treatment outcomes of ductal pancreatic adenocarcinoma. This study aimed to examine the correlation between CD86 and CD163 macrophage expression and clinical-pathological characteristics of the disease in patients operated on for pancreatic carcinoma.

title: Differential analysis of lung adenocarcinoma and lung squamous cell carcinoma based on serum tumor markers: diagnostic performance and clinical utility
creator: Zhuoying Chen, Li Chen, Lichun Wu, Ke Zhang
description: Highlights•Serum tumor markers differentiate lung adenocarcinoma from lung squamous cell carcinoma.•STM panel outperforms single markers in subtype prediction.•STM-based workflow enables non-invasive, cost-effective NSCLC subtype identification. Introduction Lung cancer remains a leading cause of cancer-related morbidity and mortality worldwide. NSCLC accounts for approximately 80%–85% of all lung cancer cases.

title: SMOKING EFFECT ON OXIDATIVE STRESS AND ANTIOXIDANT CAPACITY OF CERVICAL MUCUS IN WOMEN WITH PRIMARY IDIOPATHIC STERILITY – OBSERVATIONAL CASE-CONTROL STUDY
creator: Gordana Planinić Radoš, Željko Duić, Boris Lovrić, Josip Juras
description: SUMMARYThe aim of the study was to determine the effects of smoking on cervical mucus in women with primary idiopathic sterility. A prospective, case-control, observational, quantitative, and analytical study was carried out over a five-year period through ambulatory care. The first part of the study involved 140 healthy women (85 smokers and 55 non-smokers).

title: Readability of Online Informed Consent Forms for Implant-Based Breast Augmentation Across 6 Languages: Cross-Sectional Study
creator: Klaudia Kasperska, Tomasz Skrzypczak, Paweł Gać
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundBreast augmentation is one of the most performed aesthetic surgical procedures worldwide. Given its elective character and potential complications, clear and comprehensible informed consent is essential.ObjectiveThe aim of this paper is to evaluate and compare the readability of online informed consent forms for implant-based breast augmentation in languages used in the countries with the highest procedural volumes according to the 2024 International Society of Aesthetic Plastic Surgery (ISAPS) survey.MethodsThe phrase “breast augmentation consent form” was translated into 8 languages and searched using

title: ACUTE GENERALIZED EXANTHEMATOUS PUSTULOSIS (AGEP) CAUSED BY ANTIBIOTIC POLYTHERAPY: A CASE REPORT
creator: Siniša Jolić, Zdenka Šitum Čeprnja, Toni Čeprnja, Ognjen Jolić, Mirna Šitum
description: SUMMARYAcute generalized exanthematous pustulosis (AGEP) is a rare disease, usually associated with drug intake or infections. It is characterized by generalized acute pustules and non-follicular exanthema together with systemic symptoms. Histologically, it is characterized by a subcorneal intraepidermal spongiform pustule, papillary edema and dermal vasodilatation surrounded by a polymorphous infiltrate of neutrophils, eosinophils and mononuclear cells.

title: Repairing the Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis Trial Credibility Gap
creator: Michael Benatar, Jeffrey D. Rothstein, Kelsie Snow, Nadia Sethi, David M. Taylor, Kuldip D. Dave, Christopher J. McDermott, Thomas I. Cochrane
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). There is a long history of early- and mid-phase amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) clinical trial data being used to make claims of clinical benefit that fail to translate into successful phase 3 outcomes. It is suggested that fallacious scientific reasoning is being encouraged by perverse incentives arising from a “clinical trial industrial complex” that greatly influences trial design, data interpretation, and results communication.

title: INCIDENCE AND PREVALENCE OF INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE IN OSIJEK-BARANJA COUNTY, CROATIA, 2000-2014
creator: Marinko Žulj, Marija Raguž, Ana Petrović, Kristina Kralik, Brankica Juranić, Štefica Mikšić, Marko Boban, Robert Smolić
description: SUMMARYThe etiology of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is unknown. Data on the incidence and prevalence in different regions can help identify factors relevant to the occurrence of IBD. From 2000 to 2014, 517 patients were newly diagnosed with IBD, including 329 (63.6%) patients with ulcerative colitis (UC) and 188 (36.4%) patients with Crohn’s disease (CD).

title: Delayed submarine caldera subsidence creates extreme tsunami hazard
creator: Shane J. Cronin, Bastian Steinke, Jose C. Borrero, Emile A. Okal, Marta Ribó, Jie Wu, James D. L. White, Marco Brenna, Joali Paredes-Mariño, Mila Huebsch, Rachael Baxter, Ulrich Speidel, Alexa R. Van Eaton, Larry G. Mastin, Michael A. Clare, Isobel A. Yeo, James E. Hunt, Jacob Nash, James B. Garvin,
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The 2022 Hunga volcano eruption generated one of the largest and most destructive volcanic tsunamis ever recorded. We interpret the timing, nature and relative hazard of volcanic-tsunamigenic processes by combining geophysical, oceanographic, atmospheric, and eye-witness observations of this event. Hydro-acoustic signal (T waves) detected on seismic stations up to 2600 km away provided a key to discerning tsunami triggers from explosions, volcanic mass flows, and caldera subsidence. The largest tsunami was generated by the first of at least two sudden caldera-subsidence events.

title: ACOUSTIC RHINOMETRY STUDY IN PATIENTS WITH ALLERGIC RHINITIS
creator: Atanas Vlaykov
description: SUMMARYAcoustic rhinometry is a non-invasive technique that requires minimal cooperation from patients compared to other diagnostic methods. This technique can be used even in children under 3 years of age, which makes it widely applicable in the practice of rhinologists.

title: DIAGNOSTIC VALUE OF STIMULATED SERUM THYROGLOBULIN IN THE FOLLOW-UP OF PATIENTS WITH DIFFERENTIATED THYROID CANCER
creator: Vlado Wagenhofer, Ivan Mihaljević, Tatjana Kralj, Dubravka Vrdoljak, Tomislav Kizivat
description: SUMMARYThe aim was to determine the diagnostic value of stimulated serum thyroglobulin (sTg) for the follow-up of patients with differentiated thyroid cancer (DTC) and to evaluate whether repeated sTg measurement provides additional clinical benefit in detecting persistent or recurrent structural disease if the initial sTg was negative.

title: Biochemical production of bio-based terephthalic acid from lignocellulosic biomass for CO2 emission reduction
creator: Seiji Nakagame, Takuma Kawao, Daiki Narita, Akira Yamamura, Takeshi Noda
description: Terephthalic acid, a key precursor for polyester production, is traditionally derived from fossil resources, contributing to global warming. Although numerous studies have explored the production of terephthalic acid from biomass polysaccharides, energy-intensive chemical processes are predominantly employed. In this study, we have developed a biochemical process to produce bio-based terephthalic acid from lignocellulosic biomass for reducing CO2 emissions.

title: Assessment of the occupational exposures within homes for home healthcare workers in the United Kingdom
creator: AC Dondi, R Bellacov, M Fray, KG Davis
description: Many of the tasks being conducted by home healthcare workers are associated with significant complex demands. Each home is a unique work environment with potentially different exposures. The purpose of this study was to investigate the plethora of exposures for home healthcare workers in the United Kingdom.

title: Thermophilic site-specific recombination system for rapid insertion of heterologous DNA into the Clostridium thermocellum chromosome
creator: Nandhini Ashok, Yasemin Kaygusuz, Heidi S Schindel, Sarah Thurmon, Carrie A Eckert, Adam M Guss
description: Clostridium thermocellum is an anaerobic thermophile capable of producing ethanol and other commodity chemicals from lignocellulosic biomass. The insertion of heterologous DNA into the C. thermocellum chromosome is currently achieved via a time-consuming homologous recombination process, where a single stable insertion can take 2–4 weeks or more to construct.

title: What does Psychological Well-being Mean for Mexican Late Adolescents? A Study with Natural Semantic Networks in the Post-pandemic Era
creator: César A. García-Avitia, Sara L. Pérez-Ruvalcaba, Claudia V. Márquez-González
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundWell-being is distinguished by its complex and multifaceted characteristics, integrating both objective and subjective components, so each person’s point of view is relevant. In conducting research concerning well-being, it is important account for both age considerations and cultural variability.

title: The OsUVR8-OsNAC3-OsERF117 signaling module mediates metabolic acclimation and climate adaptation in rice
creator: Wenxin Liu, Dongxiao Zhou, Jianying Xing, Shangyong Xue, Tian-Jing Wang, Peng Guo, Yutong Liu, Zheng-Yi Xu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Ultraviolet-B (UV-B; 280 to 315 nanometers) radiation increasingly threatens crop productivity, yet the genetic basis of plant adaptation remains poorly understood. We delineate a UV-B signaling module in rice that links photoreceptor activation to transcriptional reprogramming and metabolic acclimation. The AP2/ERF transcription factor OsERF117 acts as a central regulator, directly activating flavonoid and melatonin biosynthetic genes to drive photoprotective metabolite accumulation and enhance UV-B stress tolerance.

title: Biosynthesis of guanidine-containing natural products in cyanobacteria
creator: Wenhe Zhang, Richiro Ushimaru
description: Cyanobacteria are prolific producers of structurally diverse and biologically potent natural products, a subset of which feature guanidino moieties. Introduction and modification of the guanidine group confer tuned basicity and enable extensive hydrogen bonding, cation–π, and electrostatic interactions, facilitating high-affinity binding to numerous biological targets.

title: Xyla-P Cream vs. Lidocaine Spray: Impact on Patient Satisfaction, Anxiety, Cooperation, and Pain in Spinal Anesthesia for Cesarean Section
creator: Zahra Ghalenoii, Shohreh Movahedi, Amirabbas Motezaker, Elham Ebrahimi
description: BackgroundOne of the fundamental principles of medical interventions is to avoid causing pain to patients, and childbirth is no exception. With the rising prevalence of cesarean sections, addressing factors that may diminish maternal satisfaction is crucial. Spinal anesthesia, the most common method for cesarean sections, faces challenges such as patient anxiety.

title: Density functional theory investigation of oxygen-deficient SnO2-x: Optoelectronic property tuning and hydrogen gas interaction
creator: Manoj Kumar, Purnendu Shekhar Pandey, M. Sudhakara Reddy, Anita Gehlot, Jaishanker Prasad Keshari, Akash Kumar Pradhan, Gyanendra Kumar Singh, Balkeshwar Singh, Kelong Fan, Kelong Fan, Kelong Fan, Kelong Fan
description: Oxygen-vacancy engineering is an effective strategy for tailoring the electronic, optical, and gas-sensing properties of tin dioxide (SnO2). In this work, first-principles Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations were performed to systematically investigate the influence of oxygen vacancies on the optoelectronic characteristics and hydrogen adsorption behavior of pristine SnO2 and oxygen-deficient SnO2-x. Oxygen-deficient structures were considered with SnO2-x (x = 0.

title: Engineering Streptomyces coelicolor for heterologous expression of the thiopeptide GE2270A—A cautionary tale
creator: Francesco Del Carratore, Erik K R Hanko, Kamila Schmidt, Oksana Bilyk, Suhui Ye Huang, Marianna Iorio, Mercedes Pérez-Bonilla, Rosario Pérez-Redondo, Michelle Rudden, Emmanuele Severi, Arianna Tocchetti, Margherita Sosio, Emily J Johnson, Timothy Kirkwood, Dominic R Whittall, Alkisti Manousaki, Olga
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The thiopeptide GE2270A is a clinically relevant, ribosomally synthesised, and post-translationally modified peptide naturally produced by Planobispora rosea. Due to the genetically intractable nature of P. rosea, heterologous expression is considered a possible route to yield improvement. In this study, we focused on improving GE2270A production through heterologous expression of the biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC) in the model organism Streptomyces coelicolor M1146. A statistically significant yield improvement was obtained in the S.

title: Metallo‐supramolecular nanofibers based on type‐I photosensitizer for synergistic antibacterial therapy
creator: Shibo Lyu, Lukun Li, Jingdong Gao, Dapeng Liu, Fengling Song
description: Photodynamic therapy (PDT) has shown great merits in treating microbial infections due to its absence of bacterial resistance. However, the pronounced hypoxic microenvironment in the bacterial infections limits the therapeutic efficiency of traditional type‐II PDT, which is highly dependent on oxygen. Here type‐I photosensitizer BTZn‐Py (n = 8, 20) coordinates with chemical antibacterial agent Ag+ to fabricate metallo‐supramolecular nanofibers.

title: Ensuring children's inclusion in the Bundibugyo Ebola response: Striving to do better this time
creator: Mike Kalmus Eliasz, Michael Adeyemi-Lawal, Lauren D’Mello Guyett, Daniela Manno, Bruce Myango, Paula Reges, Neal Russell
description: August 2026 where complete age and sex information is available (3454 cases and 1124 deaths) children aged 0–4 years make up 10.0% of cases, yet 19% of deaths, with an estimated case fatality rate (CFR) of 61.7% as opposed to 28.8% for those aged 18 and over [2].

title: A 5-year retrospective outlook of cardiovascular risk(s), outcome and survival peculiarities among patients in medical confinement; a tropical perspective
creator: Titilope A Bamikefa, Peter K Uduagbamen, Olanrewaju O Olayemi, Olufemi O Ojewuyi, Oyelola Adeoye, Sekinat Bola-Oyebamiji, Olubukola Ala, Abosede G Adeyeye
description: SummaryObjectiveThe study was designed to evaluate the distribution of cardiovascular risk(s), outcome modifiers and survival peculiarities among medically confined patients.DesignEvaluated admission and discharge summaries of medically confined patients retroactively over 5 years.SettingMedical wards, UniOsun Teaching Hospital Osogbo, Osun State, Nigeria.ParticipantsTwo thousand three hundred and forty (2340) male and female patients aged between 16 and 108 years.

title: Post-transcriptional regulation of Profilin-2 by microRNAs and RNA-binding proteins forms a critical regulatory node for early embryonic cell fate decisions
creator: Carolyn Sangokoya, Isabella R. Rosso, Rana Ghandehari-Alavijeh, Robert Blelloch
description: Post-transcriptional control by RNA binding proteins (RBPs) and microRNAs play central roles in mRNA stability and translation, yet how RBPs and microRNAs coordinate in developmental time to regulate cell fate remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that post-transcriptional regulation of the Profilin 2 (Pfn2) transcript is essential for differentiation of embryonic stem cells (ESCs) into the primary germ layer lineages.

title: Analyzing trends and factors influencing price changes in public pooled drugs procurement system in Malaysia: Exploring market competition
creator: Farahwahida Mohd Kasim, Ernieda Hatah, Lokhman Hakim Osman, Adliah Mhd Ali, Zaheer-Ud-Din Babar
description: BackgroundPooled procurement is key to managing drug spending amid rising healthcare costs, but conclusive evidence on its sustained impact is lacking, driven by market competition.ObjectiveThis study aims to evaluate the trends and factors influencing the price changes of drugs awarded for pooled procurement systems utilizing a drug price index analysis.

title: Breakthrough infections and incomplete vaccine efficacy drive pathogen immune escape
creator: Minjin Kim, Eunha Shim
description: IntroductionWhile vaccines effectively reduce disease severity and mortality, their consequences for pathogen immune escape remain poorly understood. Vaccines provide protection through three distinct mechanisms: prevention of infection, reduction of symptoms, and limitation of transmission. When vaccine efficacy is incomplete across multiple dimensions, breakthrough infections in vaccinated individuals may paradoxically increase pathogen escape pressure.

title: NUTCRACKER SYNDROME: A REPORT OF TWO CASES
creator: AA Adejumo, BE Osobu
description: Introduction:Nutcracker syndrome is a pathology that could pose a diagnostic conundrum to the physician as the patient could present with vague symptoms. This report brings to limelight the pathology of Nutcracker syndrome and the need for clinicians to consider this as a differential diagnosis when managing patients with non-specific abdominal pain.

title: FULL-TERM PREGNANCY IN AN INCISIONAL HERNIA: AN UNCOMMON OCCURRENCE
creator: E. Tagar, LA. Ehiagwina, OE. Oigbochie, AG. Tagar
description: Introduction:Herniation of a full-term pregnancy is a rare event that poses risks for both mothers and babies. This condition can lead to lower uterine segment rupture and intrauterine foetal death.Case presentation:We present a case of an incisional hernia with a full-term pregnancy.

title: Genetic evidence and cross-species functional characterization implicate CNN2 in age-related macular degeneration susceptibility
creator: Fei-Fei Cheng, Hao Mou, Zhenyu Liu, Chang-Jun Zhang, You-Yuan Zhuang, Zhen Wu, Xin-Ran Wen, Angli Xue, Xiao Zhang, Jian Yang, Zi-Bing Jin
description: SignificanceAge-related macular degeneration (AMD) is the most common cause of irreversible vision loss among older adults and is projected to affect approximately 288 million people worldwide by 2040. Identifying the genes and cellular mechanisms underlying established AMD risk loci is essential for understanding disease pathogenesis and facilitating therapeutic development.

title: Core components of physical activity interventions in the prevention and management of breast cancer-related lymphoedema (BCRL): A scoping review
creator: Laura Henry, Julie S. Wilson, Jason J. Wilson, Esther R. Beck, Jen Edwards, Ka Ming Chow, Ka Ming Chow, Ka Ming Chow
description: BackgroundBreast cancer-related lymphoedema, a chronic and debilitating swelling condition, can occur as a sequela of breast cancer treatment. Physical activity is a key recommendation of cancer survivorship guidelines. However, uncertainties that remain around physical activity and breast cancer-related lymphoedema management, have potentially contributed to low physical activity levels in this population.

title: Understanding the association between immune-modulating helminths and HPV or cervical cancer: A scoping review
creator: Allison Frank, Margarita Correa-Mendez, Alicia A. Livinski, Kalina Duncan, Eva H. Clark, Patti E. Gravitt, Aysegul Taylan Ozkan, Krystyna Cwiklinski, Aysegul Taylan Ozkan, Krystyna Cwiklinski, Aysegul Taylan Ozkan, Krystyna Cwiklinski, Aysegul Taylan Ozkan, Krystyna Cwiklinski, Aysegul Taylan Ozkan,
description: BackgroundCervical cancer disproportionately affects people living in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). While access to effective preventive interventions explains some of the disparity, biological causes cannot be ruled out as important contributors to the observed disparities in cervical cancer outcomes.

title: Factors influencing likelihood of participation in green social prescriptions in an international sample
creator: Nicole E. Odell, Deepti Adlakha, Katarzyna Olcoń, Michelle Kondo, Thomas Astell-Burt, Xiaoqi Feng, J. Aaron Hipp
description: Green social prescriptions (GSPs) include interventions designed to combat sedentary behavior and preventable diseases by leveraging the benefits of nature-based physical activity. As these programs are still evolving, there is limited data regarding the likelihood of participation from an international perspective.

title: Phys-Mamba: Physics-informed selective state-space fusion network for high-fidelity underwater image restoration
creator: Hongwei Li, Weishen Li, Yuqing Lao, Jie Li, Junjie He, Caihong Wu, Huilong Zhong, Shaoji Huang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Underwater image restoration is fundamental for enhancing the visual perception of Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs) and Remotely Operated Vehicles (ROVs). However, existing methods face a persistent trade-off: GAN-based approaches (e.g., FUnIE-GAN) can introduce physically inconsistent artifacts due to the absence of explicit optical constraints; Transformer architectures achieve global modeling but suffer from quadratic computational complexity O(N2), limiting their suitability for real-time multi-scale and 4K underwater imagery; and several recent Mamba-based methods still use physical or degradation priors mainly as auxiliary guidance.

title: Factors Affecting Presentation Delay to the Hospital Among Breast Cancer Patients: A Retrospective Analysis
creator: Kajal Nehra, Jisa George T, Geeta Bhardwaj, Rajesh Pasricha
description: Objective:Breast cancer constituted 13.5% of all reported new cancer in India, with a notable mortality rate due to late presentation. The current research aims to address the extent of delay in presentation to the hospital and the factors that contribute to delayed presentation among breast cancer patients.

title: Benefits and Challenges of California Offshore Wind Electricity: An Updated Assessment
creator: Adam Rose, Nathaniel Gundersen, Yamini Kumar, Joshua Jacobs, Isabel Reynoso, Najmedin Meshkati
description: Offshore wind (OSW) technology has recently been included in California’s plans to achieve 100% carbon-free electricity by 2045. As an emerging technology, many features of OSW are changing more rapidly than established renewable options and are shaped by local circumstances in unique ways that limit transferrable experiences globally.

title: TCMSF: A Construction Framework of Traditional Chinese Medicine Syndrome Ancient Book Knowledge Graph
creator: Ziling Zeng, Lin Tong, Bing Li, Wenjing Zong, Qikai Niu, Sihong Liu, Lei Zhang, Jialun Wang, Siqi Zhang, Siwei Tian, Jing'ai Wang, Wei Zhang, Huamin Zhang
description: BackgroundSyndrome is a unique and crucial concept in traditional Chinese medicine (TCM). However, much of the syndrome knowledge lacks systematic organization and correlation, and current information technologies are unsuitable for TCM ancient texts.ObjectivesWe aimed to develop a knowledge graph that presents this knowledge in a more orderly, structured, and semantically oriented manner, providing a foundation for computer-aided diagnosis and treatment.

title: Acute Myeloid Leukemia(AML) proteins for in silico drug design using pharmacophore modeling, molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulation
creator: Partho Bosu, Tonmoy Adhikary, Abu Sayed Rafi, Naveed Iqbal, Fatima Rasool, Payer Ahmed
description: Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML) is a hematological malignancy characterized by abnormal myeloid cell differentiation, disrupting normal hematopoiesis. This study utilized an integrated computational approach to identify key molecular targets and potential inhibitors for AML therapy. Analysis of the GSE9476 microarray dataset revealed 566 differentially expressed genes (DEGs), including 437 upregulated and 129 downregulated genes.

title: Using Existing Indicators to Bridge the Exposure Data Gap: A Novel Natural Hazard Assessment
creator: Adam K. Williams, James K. Summers, Linda C. Harwell
description: Extreme natural hazard events are increasing across the globe, compelling increased climate research on resiliency. Research concerning issues as integrative as climate change and natural hazard resiliency often requires complex methodologies to account for cumulative influences. Indicators can be used to parse complex data to assess the intersection of inputs and outcomes (i.e., cumulative impacts).

title: 以肠梗阻为首发症状的隐匿性乳腺癌1例
creator: 紫娟 王, 林 唐, 小辉 黄, 桃丽 王, 红月 连, 米多 谭
description: 隐匿性乳腺癌(occult breast cancer，OBC)是指体格检查、影像学检查及病理学检查均未能确认原发病灶的乳腺癌。本研究报告1例以肠梗阻为首发症状的OBC患者的临床资料。患者为67岁女性，无任何原发疾病而以肠梗阻为主要表现就诊于中南大学湘雅医学院附属株洲医院。腹部增强CT示直肠下段及升结肠增厚，肿瘤性病变可能。胸部CT示左侧腋窝多发淋巴结肿大。肠镜检查仅表现为黏膜充血、粗糙及肥厚。考虑肠道肿瘤性病变，行腹腔镜下直肠狭窄根治性切除术，术后病理诊断为直肠低分化腺癌，免疫组织化学染色结果显示雌激素受体(estrogen receptor，ER)、孕激素受体(progesterone receptor，PR)、GATA结合蛋白3(GATA binding protein 3，GATA3)、细胞角蛋白7(cytokeratin 7，CK7)表达均为阳性，考虑乳腺癌转移。乳腺MRI示双侧乳腺多发增生结节[乳腺影像报告与数据系统(breast imaging reporting and data system，BI-RADS)2]。右乳内下肿块、双侧腋窝及双侧锁骨上窝淋巴结活检结果：右乳乳腺组织未见明确癌；右侧腋窝淋巴结见小灶癌组织；左、右锁骨上窝及左腋窝淋巴结低分化癌，考虑乳腺来源。最终诊断为OBC伴淋巴结转移及直肠转移。术后16个月患者死亡。OBC通常难以找到乳腺原发病灶，OBC消化道转移尤其罕见，其临床表现往往被转移灶症状掩盖，容易被忽视，临床医生需重视；因病情进展迅速，易出现多器官损伤，预后极差，故应早期发现OBC原发病灶，以改善患者的预后。 隐匿性乳腺癌(occult breast cancer，OBC)是一种罕见特殊类型乳腺癌，发病率低、难以找到原发病灶，易漏诊、误诊。2022年中国乳腺癌的新发病例数为35.72万[1]，乳腺癌已成为女性健康首要危险因素。文献[2]报道OBC仅占所有乳腺癌的0.3%~1.0%，以腋窝淋巴结转移或转移到其他部位为首发症状，体格检查、影像学检查及病理学检查均无法发现原发病灶，诊断困难。OBC的消化道转移临床上罕见，目前报道较少，具体病因、机制及生物学行为尚不明确，容易被临床医师忽略。本文报告1例肠梗阻为首发症状的OBC的临床资料，初步探讨诊断、治疗方法，以期改善此类患者的预后。 病例资料 患者为67岁女性。因“排便困难3 d，伴腹痛5 h”于2022年5月28日就诊于中南大学湘雅医学院附属株洲医院(以下简称“我院”)。入院体格检查：腹肌无明显紧张，左下腹压痛，无反跳痛，墨菲征(-)，肝脾肋下触诊欠满意。肠鸣音较弱，约2 次/min。直肠指诊未触及明显肿块，肛门括约肌收缩可，指套退出无血染。大小便均正常，体重无明显变化。既往病史无特殊，否认家族遗传病及肿瘤史。腹部增强CT示直肠下段及升结肠增厚，肿瘤性病变可能 (图1A)。胸部CT示左侧腋窝多发淋巴结肿大 (图1B)。肠镜示距肛门约15 cm的直肠与乙状结肠交界处黏膜充血、肿胀、肥厚、粗糙，管腔变窄。病理结果示黏膜组织广泛水肿，有少许含铁血黄素，局灶充血。予抗感染、润肠通便等治疗后症状缓解，2022年6月11日应患者要求出院。 患者2022年5月的腹部CT增强扫描及胸部CT图像 Figure 1 Patient’s images of abdomen CT enhanced scan and chest CT in May 2022 A: Image of abdomen CT enhanced scan.

title: 内皮祖细胞与慢性阻塞性肺疾病：从基础研究到临床应用
creator: 雪 何, 慧卉 曾, 燕 陈
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). 慢性阻塞性肺疾病是一种以持续气流受限为特征的慢性肺部疾病，血管内皮功能障碍是其重要的发病机制之一。内皮祖细胞(endothelial progenitor cells，EPCs)作为一类具有血管修复与再生能力的祖细胞，在慢性阻塞性肺疾病的病理进程中起重要作用。慢性阻塞性肺疾病患者的外周血中EPCs数量显著减少、功能显著下降，且与疾病严重程度、肺功能下降、急性加重、营养状况及合并症等因素密切相关。吸烟、尼古丁、电子香烟及细颗粒物(particulate matter 2.5，PM2.5)等环境因素可明显损伤EPCs的功能并减少其数量，其作用机制可能涉及血管内皮生长因子/血管内皮生长因子受体、趋化因子12/趋化因子受体4信号通路及多种细胞因子的调控。此外，动物实验显示，气管内移植EPCs可明显改善肺气肿模型的肺功能及病理改变，提示靶向EPCs可能成为慢性阻塞性肺疾病治疗的关键策略之一。通过探究EPCs的动员、归巢与功能障碍的具体分子机制，探讨EPCs临床转化应用的有效性与安全性，有望为慢性阻塞性肺疾病等慢性肺部疾病的治疗提供新的思路。 慢性阻塞性肺疾病(以下简称“慢阻肺”)是一种具有高度异质性的肺部疾病，其临床特征包括咳嗽、咳痰、呼吸困难等慢性呼吸道症状，导致不可逆的肺损伤和气流受限。慢阻肺的危险因素可概括为GETomics，即遗传基因(G)、环境因素(E)及全生命期事件(T)，其中吸烟是最重要的环境暴露因素。慢阻肺的发病机制涉及气道炎症、氧化应激、细胞凋亡和组织重塑等多种病理生理过程。其中，肺血管内皮功能障碍被认为是慢阻肺发病的关键病理生理机制，主要表现为内皮细胞(endothelial cells，ECs)凋亡及血管结构的改变，这些改变可能促使肺血管重塑并引起肺动脉高压。内皮祖细胞(endothelial progenitor cells，EPCs)是一类骨髓来源的具有自我更新和定向分化潜能的细胞，在病理生理情况下被动员到外周血中，定向归巢到血管损伤区域发挥内皮修复作用。EPCs在慢阻肺的病理进程中具有重要作用。本文通过对EPCs的生物学功能及其在慢阻肺中的研究现状进行综述，旨在为慢阻肺等慢性肺部疾病的治疗提供新的思路。 EPCs的表型、鉴定及生物学功能 自Asahara等[1]在1997年首次报道外周血含有能够形成成熟ECs并具有血管新生能力的EPCs以来，EPCs在血管相关器官及疾病中的重要作用逐渐受到广泛关注。EPSs是一种源于骨髓的独特细胞亚型，其特性与胚胎造血细胞相似。这些细胞具有增殖和分化为成熟ECs的潜力，也被称为血管前体细胞[2-3]。EPCs可以被CD34、CD133和血管内皮生长因子受体(vascular endothelial growth factor receptor，VEGFR)2(在人体被称为KDR，小鼠中称为Flk-1)等表面标志物标记，通过流式细胞术或免疫荧光等技术手段进行识别[4-5]。EPCs可以从外周血、骨髓、脐带血、胎儿肝和淋巴管等多种来源中分离[6-10]。EPCs的培养通常采用外周血或骨髓单个核细胞进行体外诱导，并用对乙酰化低密度脂蛋白(acetelyated low density lipoprotein，AcLDL)和荆豆凝集素1(ulex europeaus agglutinin-1，UEA-1)的荧光染色双阳性对EPCs进行鉴定[4]。同时，体外培养的EPCs具有成管能力[11]。根据培养时间的长短，EPCs可以分为早期和晚期2种类型[5]：早期EPCs通常是指在体外培养7~10 d的细胞，具有有限的细胞增殖能力但较强的促血管生成和旁分泌活性；晚期EPCs则是指体外培养3周后的细胞，展示出较高的增殖潜力但无分泌活性。EPCs通过响应多种细胞因子、趋化因子、酶、配体和表面抗原的调节，从骨髓被招募、动员入血液循环，并归巢到受损的内皮部位以发挥其血管生成功能[12-16]。然而，关于EPCs的具体的迁移途径和信号通路，在外周循环中维持祖细胞特性以及其定位和归巢机制等方面，仍需进一步探索[17-22]。 EPCs在慢阻肺中的变化 在慢性气道疾病的病理进程中，缺氧环境被认为是动员骨髓EPCs并促进血管新生的关键因素，以期改善组织缺氧状态[23-26]。Peinado等[27]在对重度吸烟的慢阻肺患者进行研究时发现，其肺动脉中存在内皮损伤及CD133+细胞聚集，且这些细胞定位于成熟ECs附近，提示缺氧状态下祖细胞参与内皮修复过程。笔者的课题组的研究[28]和国外研究[29]均提示，与健康对照组外周血中的EPCs相比，稳定期慢阻肺患者的外周血中EPCs比例明显降低，且这种下调伴随着ECs集落的形成能力减弱、增殖能力下降以及体外一氧化氮分泌能力减弱。Salter等[30]发现慢阻肺患者血液中的EPCs数量约为健康对照者的十分之一，而其痰液中EPCs则显著增多，这表明慢阻肺患者体内的EPCs可能通过痰液被排出体外。也有学者[31]认为吸烟者和慢阻肺患者外周血EPCs存在细胞衰老表型及凋亡增加可能是外周血EPCs减少的原因。虽然一些研究结果存在差异，但是更多的临床研究支持慢阻肺患者外周血中EPCs数量减少的观点[32-39]。 在慢阻肺的不同严重程度和疾病阶段下，EPCs的数量和功能会呈现显著变化[31, 35, 38, 40-41]。研究团队[42]通过对61例慢阻肺患者与32名年龄、性别及吸烟指数匹配的健康对照者的大样本分析发现，慢阻肺患者的EPCs数量显著下调，且数量与第1秒用力呼气容积(forced expiratory volume in one second，FEV1)及FEV1占肺总量比值(forced expiratory volume in one second to forced vital capacity ratio，FEV1/FVC)呈正相关，进一步证实了气流受限的严重程度与EPCs数量呈负相关。研究团队[43]根据肺功能结果将研究参与者分为阻塞性通气功能障碍、限制性通气功能障碍与健康对照3组，对其外周血EPCs进行流式细胞分析，并结合血气分析等临床数据进行研究。结果显示，长期低氧环境下、重度阻塞性或弥散功能障碍的患者EPCs数量显著降低；此外，将血常规结果纳入分析后发现EPCs数量与红细胞计数直接相关，提示在慢性肺部疾病、长期缺氧患者中EPCs数量有显著下降。疾病严重程度越重、肺气肿程度越高的慢阻肺患者(尤其是小叶中央型肺气肿)，外周血EPCs数量越少[33-39]。这些发现强调了EPCs在不同严重程度的慢阻肺中的重要性，但仍需要在更大样本量的研究中进行进一步的验证与探讨。 研究[44-45]发现因慢阻肺急性加重而住院的患者，其循环EPCs的比例显著高于稳定期慢阻肺患者及吸烟人群，且外周血中高敏C反应蛋白和血管内皮生长因子(vascular endothelial growth factor，VEGF)的浓度和外周血EPCs比例呈正相关，一定程度上解释了慢阻肺急性加重的患者外周血EPCs数量增多的原因。此外，长期处于慢性缺氧状态的患者，其外周血中EPCs的数量明显高于非缺氧患者[43]，这表明患者的缺氧程度和氧合状态可能影响EPCs从骨髓到外周血的动员[33]。Huertas等[46]对39例中至重度慢阻肺患者[其中包括18例低体重指数(body mass index，BMI)和21例正常BMI的患者]和12例健康对照者进行研究，发现在肺功能相似的慢阻肺患者中，低BMI的亚组外周血中EPCs的细胞绝对数目明显减少，体外ECs集落的形成能力也大大减弱，这提示营养状况可能也参与了慢阻肺中EPCs减少的发病过程。在慢阻肺合并代谢综合征的人群中，EPCs有作为二者共患病标志物和治疗靶点的潜在价值[47]。慢阻肺患者运动训练后外周血中EPCs数量减少，可能是因为更多的EPCs归巢到了肺部[48]。 综上所述，在慢阻肺的疾病进程中，可能存在短期缺氧情况下EPCs功能障碍、代偿性数量上调[49]，而到了晚期出现失代偿的现象，EPCs表现出功能障碍且数量减少。随着气流阻塞、肺气肿的加剧或合并症、全身情况的改变，EPCs的数量越来越少。 慢阻肺中EPCs变化的机制 在慢阻肺中，EPCs数量的减少可能与多种机制相关，主要包括以下科学假说：骨髓产生与释放EPCs的功能受损、血管招募功能障碍、祖细胞凋亡增加、成管相关因子表达差异及细胞衰老等[31, 50]。 绝大多数假说均指向EPCs的产生、动员及功能改变的病理生理过程。多项研究[46, 50-52]显示，VEGF等促血管生成因子在多种疾病模型中均可以促进EPCs动员，参与新生血管生成的调节。VEGF可以通过VEGFR参与细胞的增殖、分化、存活等多种生物学过程[50-51]。肺动脉的免疫组织化学研究[52]显示，吸烟者和中度慢阻肺患者的VEGF表达水平增加，而在严重肺气肿的肺组织中VEGF水平则降低，提示VEGF的表达水平与慢阻肺的严重程度相关，并可能参与血管重塑过程。此外，低BMI的人群血浆中血管内皮生长因子A(vascular endothelial growth factor A，VEGFA)、血管内皮生长因子C(vascular endothelial growth factor C，VEGFC)、干细胞生长因子(stem cell growth factor，SCF)、肿瘤坏死因子(tumor necrosis factor，TNF)、白细胞介素-6(interleukin-6，IL-6)、血管生成素-1(angiopoietin-1，Ang-1)、单核细胞趋化蛋白-1(monocyte chemoattractant protein-1，MCP-1)等因子的表达水平较正常BMI的患者增高[46]。这些发现提示多种细胞因子可能参与慢阻肺中EPCs变化的病理生理过程，这些变化可能与疾病的严重程度、氧合状态、患者的营养状况等多种因素有关[46]。 趋化因子12(chemokine C-X-C motif ligand 12，CXCL12)是趋化因子家族的成员，在祖细胞的动员过程中尤其是骨髓中CD34+细胞的动员中发挥重要作用，是首个被报道的祖细胞趋化因子[53]。趋化因子受体4(chemokine C-X-C motif receptor 4，CXCR4)是CXCL12的特异性配体，其同EPCs显示出一致的变化模式，表明CXCL12及其受体CXCR4在祖细胞的迁移和功能中扮演重要角色[30]。在体外培养的慢阻肺患者外周血EPCs中，CXCR4的表达显著下调[54]。CXCL12/CXCR4信号轴可能是骨髓祖细胞动员的关键通路之一[55]。在慢阻肺模型小鼠中也观察到骨髓微环境中CXCL12/CXCR4通路表达的明显降低，进一步证明了此通路在慢阻肺病理过程中的关键作用[56]。 综上，VEGF/VEGFR、CXCL12/CXCR4通路及相关细胞因子的调节可能在慢阻肺的EPCs相关发病机制中扮演重要角色，其详细机制和潜在的治疗靶点仍需通过更多研究来深入探索。 其他危险因素对EPCs的影响 吸烟 吸烟是慢阻肺最常见的危险因素。关于吸烟是否在慢阻肺状态发生之前就已经造成了EPCs的改变，仍需更多的探讨[37,

title: 治疗前外周血血红蛋白×淋巴细胞/单核细胞水平对鼻咽癌患者预后的影响
creator: Chao DENG, Zui CHEN, Jie LING, Yangchun XIE, Xiayan ZHAO, Chunhong HU, Xianling LIU, Yuhua FENG, Tao HOU, 敏宁 彭
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). 目的外周全血细胞计数可作为多种肿瘤的预后预测因子，但其在鼻咽癌预后中的预测价值仍未可知。本研究探讨治疗前外周血血红蛋白×淋巴细胞/单核细胞(hemoglobin×lymphocyte/monocyte ratio，HLMR)水平对接受根治性放疗的非复发转移性鼻咽癌患者预后的影响。方法回顾性分析805例完成根治性放疗或放化疗的鼻咽癌患者的临床病理资料及随访记录，收集患者治疗前的外周血血红蛋白、淋巴细胞计数和单核细胞计数结果，计算HLMR值，绘制受试者操作特征(receiver operating characteristic，ROC)曲线，并判定患者HLMR的最佳临界值；根据最佳临界值，将患者分为高HLMR组和低HLMR组，使用χ 2检验分析HLMR与患者临床病理特征的关系；使用Cox风险模型确定影响鼻咽癌患者总生存期和无进展生存期的独立危险因素。根据独立危险因素建立诺莫图，预测患者的生存率，并利用验证队列进行内部验证。结果ROC曲线显示HLMR对鼻咽癌患者5年生存率的最佳临界值为605.5，多因素Cox回归分析显示：T分期(HR=1.886，95% CI 1.331~2.673，P<0.001)，N分期(HR=2.021，95% CI 1.267~3.225，P=0.003)，美国东部肿瘤协作组(Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group，ECOG)评分(HR=3.991，95% CI 1.257~12.677，P=0.019)，同步放化疗模式(HR=0.338，95% CI 0.156~0.731，P=0.006)，HLMR(HR=0.648，95% CI 0.460~0.912，P=0.013)为患者总生存期的独立预后因素。在训练队列中，纳入T分期、N分期、HLMR等因素建立诺莫图预测患者3、5和7年的总生存率，该模型的C-index为0.713，其对患者3、5和7年生存率预测的曲线下面积分别为0.744、0.665和0.682，校正曲线分析表明该模型预测的患者生存率与实际观察到的患者生存率具有较好的一致性。上述结果在验证队列中得到进一步证明。结论治疗前HLMR可能是一个有潜力的鼻咽癌患者预后预测标志物。Keywords: 血红蛋白×淋巴细胞/单核细胞, 鼻咽癌, 生存率, 临床病理特征, 预后标志物 鼻咽癌(nasopharyngeal carcinoma，NPC)是原发于鼻咽部的恶性肿瘤，发病与EB病毒感染密切相关，具有明显的地区流行性，全球有近一半的病例发生在中国[1]。新发NPC患者中，局部晚期患者占70%以上，标准治疗以放化疗为主[2]。经过标准方案治疗后，15%~30%的局晚期NPC患者最终出现复发或转移[3]。因此，研究影响NPC预后的因素对改善NPC患者的预后具有十分重要的意义。研究[4]表明炎症反应与肿瘤的发生、发展及预后密切相关。激活的免疫细胞通过诱导DNA损害、干扰DNA修复从而加速肿瘤进展[5]。其中，外周全血细胞计数能够反映潜在的炎症反应，是研究热点之一。外周血免疫指标包括血小板、血红蛋白、中性粒细胞、淋巴细胞、单核细胞、巨噬细胞等。研究[6-10]证实中性粒细胞和淋巴细胞比值(neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio，NLR)、血小板和淋巴细胞比值(platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio，PLR)、系统性免疫炎症指数(systemic immune inflammation index，SII)、系统性炎症反应指数(systemic inflammation response index，SIRI)能够作为多种肿瘤的预后预测因子。血红蛋白、淋巴细胞和单核细胞比值能够预测多种肿瘤(包括NPC)的预后[11-12]。外周血血红蛋白×淋巴细胞/单核细胞(hemoglobin×lymphocyte/monocyte，HLMR)是一个新的组合指标，其在NPC中的预后价值尚无文献报道。 本研究通过回顾性分析805例完成根治性放疗或放化疗的NPC患者的临床病理资料及随访记录，分析HLMR作为预测非复发转移性NPC预后的可行性，旨在应用HLMR对NPC患者进行预后分层。 资料与方法 临床资料 选取2013年1月至2019年12月中南大学湘雅二医院收治的接受根治性放疗或放化疗的初治NPC患者805例。纳入标准：1)经组织病理学确诊为NPC；2)接受根治性调强适形放疗；3)有治疗前完整的影像学检查结果及血常规结果。排除标准：1)未完成放疗计划；2)治疗前有出血、贫血、感染、肝肾功能不全等合并症；3)有免疫系统、血液系统及其他恶性肿瘤等合并症；4)治疗前半个月内使用激素治疗(患者纳入、排除流程见图1)。 患者纳入和排除流程图 Figure 1 Consort diagram for patient inclusion and exclusion 收集所有入组患者治疗前的人口学信息、临床信息等，包括年龄、性别、身高、体重、美国东部肿瘤协作组(Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group，ECOG)评分、T分期、N分期、临床分期、治疗方案、外周血血红蛋白、外周血淋巴细胞、单核细胞计数及随访信息等，建立数据库进行分析。本研究已获得中南大学湘雅二医院伦理委员会的批准(伦审[临研]第092号)。 治疗方法 放疗 所有患者均采用调强放疗技术，接受直线加速器6 MV-X线照射。根据ICRU50号及ICRU62号报告的原则进行靶区勾画。鼻咽部原发灶剂量70 Gy/31~33次，颈部淋巴结转移灶剂量70 Gy/31~33次，亚临床病灶及高危淋巴结引流区剂量60 Gy/31~33次，低危淋巴结引流区剂量54~56 Gy/31~33次。根据RTOG0225的原则勾画危及器官及限定剂量。 诱导及辅助化疗 所有III~IVa期及部分II期患者接受1~3个疗程的诱导化疗，诱导化疗方案：以顺铂或奈达铂为基础的双药方案。根据患者临床分期及放疗后复查情况，部分患者接受1~2周期含铂双药化疗或单药卡培他滨化疗。 同期化疗 根据患者临床分期及耐受性，部分患者放疗同期采用顺铂或奈达铂 100 mg/m2，每3~4周为1周期，共1~3周期。 随访 治疗结束后的1年内每3个月复查1次，1年后每6个月复查1次，5年后每年复查1次，采用电话、门诊或住院方式进行随访。末次随访时间为2023年4月30日。主要研究终点为总生存期(overall survival，OS)，次要研究终点为无进展生存时间(progression free survival，PFS)。OS定义为治疗开始至患者死亡的时间，PFS定义为治疗开始至疾病进展或患者死亡的时间。 观察指标 收集患者治疗前72 h内的血常规结果，记录血红蛋白、淋巴细胞计数及单核细胞计数等数值，计算HLMR。 统计学处理 采用SPSS 26.0统计学软件及R软件(4.1.3版)进行数据分析。HLMR的最佳临界值采用受试者操作特征(receiver operating characteristic，ROC)曲线确定，依据约登指数确定HLMR的最佳临界值。HLMR与各临床病理学参数间的相关性采用χ 2检验，采用Kaplan-Meier法计算生存率，生存率的组间差别采用Log-rank检验。采用Cox回归模型进行多因素分析，P<0.05为差异有统计学意义。最后，纳入Cox回归分析中的独立预后因素建立诺莫图，并检验其对患者OS和PFS的预测效能。 结 果 患者临床资料的基线特征

title: Influence of mobile phone calls on the compliance of the recommended four antenatal care visits in Kisii County, Kenya: a cluster randomized control trial
creator: Zillah M Malachi, Lucy W Kivuti-Bitok, Anna K Karani, Joyce J Cheptum
description: BackgroundAntenatal care attendance is still low in sub-Saharan countries. While mobile phones have shown to improve outcomes in maternal health services, there are few published studies on the use of mobile phone calls in antenatal care.ObjectiveTo determine the influence of mobile phone calls on pregnant women's completion of the recommended 4 ANC visits in Kisii County, Kenya.

title: Evaluation of the Association between Smoking and Tonsillolith Characteristics Using Cone-Beam Computed Tomography
creator: Ali Rasat, Sevcihan Günen Yılmaz
description: ObjectiveTonsilloliths are calcified concretions within tonsillar crypts whose relationship with smoking remains poorly understood. This study investigated the association between smoking and tonsillolith characteristics using cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT).Subject and MethodsThis retrospective cross-sectional study evaluated 416 dental CBCT scans obtained between 2021 and 2023.

title: Efficacy of midnight-noon Ebb-flow hour-prescription method combined with acupuncture at Baihui Bazhen acupoints in the rehabilitation of Aphasia after ischemic stroke
creator: Yunbo Li, Chaoqi Lu, Lin Chen
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundTo investigate the clinical effectiveness of combining the midnight-noon ebb-flow hour-prescription method with acupuncture at the Baihui (GV 20) and Bazhen acupoints for rehabilitating aphasia following ischemic stroke.Methodology196 patients with aphasia after ischemic stroke were divided into two groups: a research group (n=98) that received language rehabilitation training along with the midnight-noon ebb-flow hour-prescription method and acupuncture at Baihui (GV 20) Bazhen acupoints, and a control group (n=98) that received only language rehabilitation training.

title: PMAxx dye-assisted colorimetric dual DNAzyme-LAMP (PD-cDDLAMP) for rapid phenotypic antimicrobial susceptibility testing of Escherichia coli
creator: Alaa H. Sewid, Joseph H. Ramos, Benti D. Gelalcha, Yuri Matsuoka, Oudessa Kerro Dego, Shigetoshi Eda
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Rapid antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST) is crucial for combating antimicrobial resistance and guiding effective therapy. Conventional phenotypic AST methods are often time-consuming, requiring 18–72 h for results, while genotypic approaches often depend on pre-existing knowledge of resistance markers. Although nucleic acid-based phenotypic AST methods have reduced turnaround time, attempts to shorten antibiotic exposure often produce only small differences between susceptible and resistant bacteria.

title: Recent updates on molecular epidemiology of hepatitis C virus in Gujranwala, Pakistan
creator: Bacha Syed Yousuf Shah, Khan Muhammad Umer, Zulfiqar Aymn, Zahid Tazeen, Ghani Muhammad Usman, Amin Iram, Shahid Muhammad, Munir Rakhtasha, Younas Saima, Vajeeha Ayesha
description: BackgroundHepatitis C infection (HCV) remains a leading cause of liver cirrhosis, posing a critical health threat worldwide.ObjectiveThis research aimed to provide a contemporary overview of HCV infection and its genotypic distribution in Gujranwala, Punjab, Pakistan. Additionally, it sought to explore the interrelation between HCV genotypes and associated risk factors among individuals infected with HCV.

title: Male adolescents' (Aged 15-24 years) smoking habit and its determinant: analysis of Indonesia demographic and health survey data, 2017
creator: Diana Rohmandani Putri, Erni Astutik, Putri Bungsu Machmud, Tika Dwi Tama
description: ObjectivesThe aim of the study was to examine the factors influencing cigarette consumption among male adolescents aged 15-24 years in Indonesia.MethodsThis study used the Indonesia Demographics and Health Survey 2017, which included 8,488 male adolescents aged 15-24 years. The survey used multi-stage cluster sampling. Data were analyzed by using multivariable logistic regression adjusted for covariates and a complex survey design.

title: The effectiveness of COVID-19 Heterologous Vaccination: the experience from a Regional Hospital in Cameroon
creator: Princewill Kum Unji, Alex Mambap Tatang, Samuel Angwafor, Loveline Lum Niba, Adji Minette Jaqueline Porro, Denis Nsame Nforniwe, Andreas Chiabi
description: BackgroundWith most COVID-19 vaccines requiring at least 2 doses, heterologous vaccination will facilitate vaccination programs where vaccine supplies fluctuate. However, with insufficient data on effects of heterologous vaccination in our setting, people remain reluctant to mix.ObjectivesWe seek to assess the effects of heterologous vaccination on morbidity and mortality.

title: Divergent coronaviruses discovered in the virome of lamprey with reddening syndrome
creator: Jessica A. Darnley, Stephanie J. Waller, Rebecca K. French, Riki Parata, Karthiga Kumanan, Luka Finn, Jonah L. Yick, Jane Kitson, Patrick Cahill, Ian Davidson, Ryan Hunter, Benjamin W. Neuman, Kate S. Hutson, Jemma L. Geoghegan
description: Lamprey reddening syndrome (LRS) is an emerging disease affecting pouched lamprey (Geotria australis; kanakana/piharau), a culturally and ecologically significant species in Aotearoa, New Zealand. Characterized by skin hemorrhaging and elevated mortality, the etiology of LRS has remained unresolved despite previous investigations.

title: Research progress on the role of ginsenoside Rd in central nervous system diseases
creator: Xiaoyu Ma, Juejin Wang
description: Ginsenoside Rd (GSRd) is one of the rare saponin monomers extracted from ginseng. Most importantly, GSRd could effectively cross the intact blood-brain barrier (BBB). Studies have shown that it plays an important role in the treatment of neurological diseases such as ischemic stroke (IS), spinal cord injury (SCI), Alzheimer's disease (AD) and Parkinson's disease (PD).

title: Comparative evaluation of screening approaches for antiviral monoclonal antibody combinations
creator: Maria K. McClave, Samantha K. Marzi, Ekaterina E. Heldwein
description: Monoclonal antibody (mAb) cocktails are increasingly used as antiviral therapeutics, but methods for evaluating mAb combination effects remain poorly standardized. To characterize interactions of recently isolated neutralizing mAbs targeting human cytomegalovirus glycoprotein B, we compared three screening approaches: checkerboard neutralization assays; DiaMOND, a high-throughput small-molecule interaction screening tool modified for mAb combinations; and EMERALD, a modified variable-ratio framework.

title: The Luganda Edinburgh Postnatal depression scale: cross-cultural adaptation and validation for prenatal screening of depression in a Ugandan sample
creator: David Christopher Mukasa, Sam Ononge, Imelda Namagembe, Josaphat Byamugisha, Musa Sekikubo, Mark Muyingo, Noeline Nakasujja
description: BackgroundDepression affects approximately 364 million people globally. Prenatal depression affects between 26.3% and 32.9% of mothers in Africa. Opportunities for prenatal screening are missed. The gold standard diagnostic, the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders-Fifth edition (DSM-5) criteria for Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) has higher technical requirement.

title: Comparative transcriptome and proteome analysis of resistant and susceptible Talaromyces marneffei clinical isolates reveals a systemic multitiered defense network against azoles
creator: Zheng Yanqing, Peng Gaoyuan, Pang Xiaofeng, Liang Chaojuan, Luo Xiaolu, Wei Cailing, Qin Jianglong, Zou Jun, Wang Zhiyi, Pan Kaisu, Du Mingwei, Xue Peng, Liao Wanqing, Yu Mei
description: Talaromyces marneffei is a thermally dimorphic fungus causing life-threatening systemic mycosis in immunocompromised patients. The emergence of azole-resistant clinical isolates, especially those with reduced susceptibility to voriconazole (VOC) and fluconazole (FLC), presents a critical therapeutic challenge. Although target-gene alterations and efflux-related mechanisms have been reported in pathogenic fungi, the broader molecular basis distinguishing high-minimum-inhibitory concentration (MIC) and low-MIC T.

title: Factors influencing the development of osteoporosis in elderly patients with rheumatoid arthritis
creator: Yanru Yang, Ying Chen, Li Zhang, Xiaofeng Yang, Jingquan Qiao
description: BackgroundTo explore the influencing factors of osteoporosis (OP) in elderly patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA).MethodologyA total of 145 elderly patients with RA were divided into comorbidity group (with OP) of 79 patients and RA group (without OP) of 66 patients. Demographic data and laboratory parameters were collected from patients. Demographic characteristics and laboratory parameters were compared between the two groups.

title: A Clinical AI-Based System (MoodMon) for Affective Disorders: Algorithm Development and Validation
creator: Marlena Sokół-Szawłowska, Łukasz Święcicki, Katarzyna Kolasa, Katarzyna Kaczmarek-Majer, Bradley Malin
description: BackgroundPsychiatry needs objective technological tools to address global staffing shortages, stigma, and other systemic challenges. An AI-based system for mood monitoring (MoodMon) was developed along with a mobile app for smartphones to detect changes in the mental state of individuals with major depressive disorder (MDD) and bipolar disorder (BD) based on acoustic features derived from speech signals.

title: Risk factors for invasive mold infection after COVID-19: case-control study
creator: Esma Eryilmaz-Eren, Hafize Sav, Zuhal Ozer-Simsek, İbrahim Ozcan, Aysin Kilinc-Toker, Azade Kanat, Ali Cetinkaya, Recep Civan Yuksel, Kaniye Aydin, Seda Guzeldag, Ilhami Celik
description: BackgroundInvasive mold infections (IMI) have become common in patients with severe COVID-19 pneumonia, which are difficult to diagnose and treat, with a high mortality rate.ObjectiveThe aim of this study was to determine risk factors for invasive mold infections associated with COVID-19.

title: Early mechanical changes of limb muscle in septic shock assessed by dual-plane shear-wave elastography
creator: Ivo Neto Silva, Rui Azevedo, Joana Duarte, Stanislas Abrard, José Alberto Duarte, Karim Bendjelid
description: BackgroundSeptic shock induces skeletal muscle wasting and neuromuscular dysfunction, contributing to ICU-acquired weakness (ICUAW) and poor recovery after critical illness. Conventional ultrasound primarily captures structural changes but provides limited insight into early muscle mechanical alterations or their relationships with clinical factors. Shear-wave elastography (SWE) enables non-invasive assessment of muscle stiffness, but its performance in critically ill patients remains poorly understood.

title: An overview of key industrial product citric acid production by Aspergillus niger and its application
creator: Ambreen Latif, Noor Hassan, Hazrat Ali, Muhammad Bilal Khan Niazi, Zaib Jahan, Iqra Latif Ghuman, Farwa Hassan, Anam Saqib
description: Citric acid possesses high economic value and is considered as the world’s largest consumed organic acid in numerous industries. Citric acid applications range from food to beverage industries, pharmaceuticals, cosmetics, and the environment. It is mostly produced by microbial fermentation, but Aspergillus niger is considered as the main workhorse for large-scale production of citric acid.

title: Beyond living donation: robot-assisted kidney transplantation using deceased-donor grafts—a scoping review of selection, ischaemia logistics, and allograft outcomes
creator: Rafał Bogdan Drobot, Tomasz Domel, Marcin Lipa, Daniel Ludwiczak
description: Deceased-donor robot-assisted kidney transplantation (DD-RAKT) couples an unscheduled graft pathway with a resource-dependent operation. Living-donor-dominated reviews do not resolve DD-specific selection, ischaemia logistics, outcomes, or patient benefit. We aimed to map DD-RAKT selection, preservation-to-reperfusion logistics, outcomes, and the limits of inference about patient benefit.

title: Finding of the positive impact of glucose on the production of indican over indigo in engineered Escherichia coli
creator: Hyun Jin Kim, Yeda Lee, Yuni Shin, Suhye Choi, Jinok Oh, Suwon Kim, Jungoh Ahn, Kwon-Young Choi, Jeong Chan Joo, Shashi Kant Bhatia, Yung-Hun Yang
description: Indigo is a plant-based natural blue dye that can be produced via chemical synthesis and biological pathways. However, the toxic reduction processes and intracellular production of indigo through microbial metabolism are often limited by insolubility of indigo and complex downstream processing, causing environmental issues in the dyeing processes.

title: Beyond vein diameter: pain phenotyping complements updated diagnostic criteria for female pelvic venous disorders
creator: Vinicius Adami Vayego Fornazari, Renato Abu Hana, Grit Armstrong Adler, Sara Lojo-Lendoiro, Nucelio Lemos, Gregory Kirk Lewis, Jean-Pierre Pelage, Gloria Maria Salazar
description: men and loses diagnostic value after adjustment for proximal venous outflow obstruction (VOO) and superficial varicosities [1]. Their findings represent more than a refinement of imaging criteria; they challenge the traditional assumption that pelvic venous disorders can be diagnosed primarily from venography or cross-sectional imaging.

title: A nomogram based on preoperative NLR predicts distant metastasis of urothelial carcinoma of the bladder
creator: Xingxing Zhang, Bin Zhang, Yang He, Wei Xiong, Yuelin Du, Panfeng Shang
description: BackgroundDistant metastasis (DM) remains the most commonly reported cause of death in patients with urothelial carcinoma of the bladder (UCB).ObjectiveWe aimed to develop a robust prognostic model to assess the risk of DM in patients with UCB.MethodsWe collected clinical data of 206 UCB patients treated with RC.

title: Allee Effect and Oncolytic Virotherapy: Different Therapeutic Outcomes for Different Tumour Growth
creator: Jiawen Chen, Federico Frascoli, Tonghua Zhang
description: Tumour recurrence after oncolytic virotherapy is a critical clinical challenge, as solid cancers tend to persist and spread after such therapies alone. Often, mathematical models consider tumour growth without taking possible cooperative cell behaviours into account. Instead, the well-known Allee effect has the ability to drive low-density tumour dynamics and affect therapeutic outcomes.

title: Effectiveness of Chamomile in Reducing the Incidence and Severity of Nausea and Vomiting After Middle Ear Surgery: A Triple-Blind Randomized Study
creator: Maryam Sarkhosh, Ehsan Rajabi Visroodi, Hamidreza Samaee, Motahareh Farhadi, Parisa Moradimajd
description: BackgroundNausea and vomiting are among the most common complications after surgery. ObjectivesThe aim of this study was to investigate the effectiveness of chamomile in reducing the incidence and severity of nausea and vomiting after middle ear surgery. MethodsA total of 110 patients who met the inclusion criteria were randomly assigned to either the chamomile or placebo group.

title: A Microglial Regulatory Program Linked to Neuropsychiatric Disorders
creator: Dimitri Traenkner, Alyssa P. Johnson, Megan E. Williams, Adrian Rothenfluh
description: Hoxb8 is a transcription factor required for the normal function of a specialized microglial population. Loss of Hoxb8 causes compulsive overgrooming and anxiety-like behaviors in mice, with greater severity in females after sexual maturity. However, the Hoxb8-dependent transcriptional program in microglia remains poorly understood.

title: Proteome-wide crosslinking mass spectrometry reveals novel components of essential complexes in Toxoplasma
creator: Simon Butterworth, Ashley L. Gin, Shikha Shikha, Isadonna Tengganu, John Rush, Tom Duraisingh, Victoria Sodeinde, Leandro Lemgruber, Fabian Schulte, Ke Hu, Lilach Sheiner, Sergey Ovchinnikov, Sebastian Lourido
description: Protein–protein interactions underpin nearly all cellular processes, yet systematic definition of these networks remains limited outside a few model organisms. As a result, the architectures of essential complexes in many divergent lineages remain poorly characterized. Here we developed a high-coverage crosslinking mass spectrometry framework to map the proteome-wide interactome of the model apicomplexan parasite Toxoplasma gondii .

title: A fiducial-based framework for precise MRI-guided stereotaxic targeting in nonhuman primates
creator: Peyton Harmon, Reza Azadi
description: BackgroundAccurate MRI-guided stereotaxic targeting in nonhuman primates requires reliable registration between MRI coordinates and stereotaxic space. We evaluated skull-fixed MR-compatible screw fiducials as a practical reference for this registration.ResultsUsing a 3D-printed skull model with 28 fiducials and three internal targets, we compared offset translation, rigid registration, and affine registration under aligned and misaligned conditions.

title: GLORB: Robust Bayesian inference for differential expression under global expression shifts
creator: Rowan Callahan, Stephen D. Coleman, Thuy T. M. Ngo
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Estimating differential gene expression is a common task in RNA-seq. Current methods mostly rely on normalization to reduce variance and increase accuracy. These methods are widely used and provide invaluable information about transcriptomic changes between biological conditions. However, widely used normalization methods are known to distort estimates of transcript differential expression when a majority of genes are upregulated or downregulated, or when the total RNA content per cell changes.

title: Exploring the interaction between extracellular matrix components of bone marrow and prostate cancer cells in a novel 3D model
creator: Jianhui Yang, Peter Van Veldhuizen, Hani Awad, Hiroshi Miyamoto, Wojciech Wojciechowski, Kathleen Gillespie, Brian Marples, Omar Aljitawi
description: Our study aims to investigate the interaction between disseminated prostate cancer (PC) cells and the extracellular matrix (ECM) of the bone marrow microenvironment (BMM) using a 3Dimensional (3D) in vitro model, which biochemically resembles the stromal ECM part of the hematopoietic stem cell niche. Wharton's Jelly (WJ) was processed and lyophilized to produce a decellularized WJ matrix (DWJM).

title: Sensory cortical disinhibition is required for long-term fear memory in humans
creator: Joshua A Brown, Yijia Ma, Yifan Wang, John J Massa, Peter Kuan-Hao Cheng, Chaowen Chen, Mingzhou Ding, Norman B Schmidt, Mohammed R Milad, Jair C Soares, Raymond J Dolan, Chenyu You, Wen Li
description: The transformation of transient threats into enduring memories is fundamental to survival, yet how the human brain constructs long-term fear memory remains elusive. Early sensory cortex, traditionally viewed as a passive feature analyzer, is increasingly recognized as an active participant in fear processing.

title: An adaptive time-tree transition kernel for Bayesian phylogenetic inference
creator: Marius Brusselmans, Guy Baele, Samuel L. Hong, Jiansi Gao, Marc A. Suchard, Andrew Rambaut, Luiz Max Carvalho
description: Bayesian phylogenetic and phylodynamic analyses can be very time-consuming, owing to the combination of complex models that are used to estimate key parameters from increasingly large genomic data sets and their associated metadata. The use of high-performance computer hardware can -- to a certain extent -- alleviate the computational burden and markedly decrease the time to results.

title: Ultrasound-shear-assisted enzymatic preparation of α-glucosidase inhibitory peptides from Juglans sigillata D. and elucidation of their molecular inhibitory mechanism
creator: Xingjing Zhang, Boxiao Wu, Baitong Zhu, Zhongxing Chu, Quankang Liu, Chang Zou, Ting Ma, Feijun Luo, Yaping Zhou, Delu Ning
description: Graphical abstractKeywords: Juglans sigillata D., Ultrasound-shear-assisted enzymatic hydrolysis, α-Glucosidase-inhibitory peptides, α-Glucosidase inhibitory activity Introduction Globally, type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) has emerged as a pervasive chronic metabolic disorder. The disruption of postprandial glucose homeostasis is recognized as a critical determinant of systemic metabolic health [1], [2].

title: Clinical research advances in pulmonary infections in 2025: a narrative review of multipathogen assessment, precision diagnosis, and integrated management
creator: Xiang Luo, Zhengtu Li, Feng Ye
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background and ObjectiveThe diagnosis and treatment of pulmonary infections have become increasingly complex owing to antimicrobial resistance, the growing population of immunocompromised patients, and the ongoing circulation of respiratory viruses. In this narrative review, the major clinical advances reported in 2025 are summarised, and evidence-based support for multipathogen assessment, precision diagnosis, individualized treatment, and integrated management of pulmonary infections is provided.MethodsPubMed, Web of Science, and the Chinese Medical Association Journal Database were searched for relevant English-language and Chinese-language publications.

title: Failure Modes of Screw Fixation in Slipped Capital Femoral Epiphysis: A Proposed Life-Cycle Classification
creator: Graydon Dietrich, Zayne Browning, Jerard Tambunan, Ryan Dieter, Kurt Soloniuk, Dewayne Weaver
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Screw fixation is the standard surgical treatment for slipped capital femoral epiphysis. Screw-related adverse events, including implant breakage, joint penetration, fixation failure, growth-mediated construct change, removal failure, and postremoval fracture, are inconsistently reported throughout the pediatric orthopaedic literature. In this current concept review, we propose a practical, life-cycle classification encompassing implant insertion, in vivo fixation, growth and remodeling, implant removal, and postremoval follow-up. Reported screw-related failures cluster into four practical evidence domains: placement-related risk, construct-longevity failure, mechanical implant failure, and removal/postremoval complications.

title: Selumetinib for pediatric arteriovenous malformation with a MAP2K1 variant identified by liquid biopsy of nidus-draining venous blood
creator: Daichi Hayashi, Michio Ozeki, Akifumi Nozawa, Shiho Yasue, Saori Endo, Hiroshi Kawada, Masayuki Matsuo, Toshiaki Ishida, Hidenori Ohnishi
description: etwork. Somatic gain-of-function mutations in the RAS/MAPK signaling pathway are a major cause of extracranial AVMs.1 An integrated analysis of 4 genetic studies encompassing 101 AVM patients demonstrated that MAP2K1 was the most frequently mutated gene, accounting for 40.6% of cases.2 Mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase (MEK) inhibitors have emerged as a promising targeted therapy for AVMs harboring RAS/MAPK pathway mutations.

title: Human T cell engineering via serial delivery of mRNA encapsulated within lipid nanoparticles
creator: Apoorva Ramamurthy, Giulia Scimonelli, William L Murphy, Krishanu Saha
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Human T cells modified with nucleic acids constitute a powerful and emerging therapeutic modality for cancer, autoimmune disorders, and aging-related diseases. However, delivering nucleic acids, such as mRNA encoding synthetic receptors, transcription factors, cytokines, or genome editors to T cells can be challenging, as nucleic acids can unintentionally reduce viable T cell yield and function, particularly when delivered sequentially ex vivo.

title: Biallelic ABCG8 Variants or Biochemical Evidence of Sitosterolemia: A Case Report
creator: Joseph Burns, Justin Zachariah
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Sitosterolemia is a rare lipid disorder characterized by xanthomas, premature atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD), and abnormally elevated circulating low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-c) measurements. Pathogenic variants in adenosine triphosphate (ATP)-binding cassette transporters lead to the accumulation of phytosterols. A child presented to the pediatric cardiology clinic with an incidentally noted presumed pathogenic variant and a variant of unknown significance in a sitosterolemia gene but had normal fasting lipids and no accumulation of circulating phytosterols.

title: Adoption, Perceived Barriers, and Future Perspectives of Guided Endodontics for the Management of Calcified Root Canals Among Endodontists: A Cross-Sectional Questionnaire-Based Study
creator: Mohd Zeeshan Ahmad, Krishna P Biswas, Diwakar Vasisth, Aarti S Bedia, Sanpreet S Sachdev, Anil Richhawal
description: Introduction: Guided endodontics has emerged as a promising digital approach for the management of calcified root canals by improving the accuracy of canal localization and minimizing procedural complications. Despite its clinical advantages, information regarding its adoption and factors influencing its implementation among endodontists remains limited.

title: Insights Into Chikungunya Virus Seropositivity and Clinical Manifestations During the 2024 Upsurge: A Study From Central India
creator: Vishal Shete, Meena Mishra, Omna Nelumbium, Rashmi Mudliar, Bharatsing D Rathod, Nishaant Ramasamy, Preeti A Shahu, Shailendra Parihar
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundChikungunya remains a significant threat to public health in India, characterised by repeated resurgences. This study was conducted to describe the demographic and clinical profile and associated complications among chikungunya patients during the 2024 upsurge.MethodsThis retrospective observational study included patients with acute febrile illness who tested positive for chikungunya immunoglobulin M (IgM) using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) between January and December 2024.
